data.title: TradFi News | Ark Invest Buys $90 Million of Anthropic Shares on Record IPO Debut, Trims Nvidia
data.description:
Cathie Wood’s Ark Invest bought more than $90 million of Anthropic stock on the AI company’s first day of trading on Nasdaq, according to Ark’s trading update. The firm bought about 935,000 shares across six funds on Thursday, November 19, and sold about 33,430 Nvidia shares worth $4.9 million. Anthropic raised $81.3 billion by selling 980 million shares at $83 each, topping SpaceX’s $75 billion June listing as the largest IPO on record, according to CoinDesk.
ARKK Accounts for Most of Ark’s Anthropic Purchase
Ark’s flagship ARK Innovation ETF (ARKK) bought 556,777 Anthropic shares, about 60% of the firm’s total purchase and worth roughly $54 million at Thursday’s close (calculated). The rest was split across five other Ark funds.

Despite the purchase, Anthropic sits outside Ark’s top 10 holdings. Those are led by Tesla, SpaceX, Tempus AI and Amazon.
The Anthropic buy is far smaller than Ark’s SpaceX trade. On SpaceX’s IPO day in June, Ark bought 3.3 million shares worth about $500 million.
Anthropic Closes 17% Above IPO Price After Volatile Debut
Anthropic, which trades under the ticker ANT, priced its shares at $83, above its $70–$78 range, and opened at $111.50. The stock closed at $97.17, up 17.1% from the IPO price (calculated). That was 13% below the open and 16% below the intraday high. Almost 850 million shares changed hands on the first day.

Ark Sells Nvidia as Shares Keep Falling
Ark sold about 33,430 Nvidia shares on the same day, worth about $4.9 million at the close. Nvidia ended Thursday at $145.98, down about 4% from Wednesday. The company is led by interim CEO Colette Kress following Jensen Huang’s departure on November 12.
Nvidia shares have fallen since the company’s earnings beat on Tuesday. UBS cut its price target to $220 from $240, its second cut in three days, and JPMorgan analysts said the results did not resolve concerns over AI demand and financing.

data.title: Binance Extends USD1 Rewards Campaign With Estimated APR Up to 10%
data.description: Binance announced on X that it has extended its USD1 rewards campaign and expanded the reward pool. Users who hold USD1 in any account can receive an estimated APR of up to 10%.

data.title: GaoTeng Bitcoin ETF Lists on Hong Kong Stock Exchange as New Huo Invests About $10 Million
data.description: The GaoTeng Bitcoin ETF listed on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange today, with New Huo Group participating in its cornerstone investment with about $10 million. According to Foresight News, New Huo Asset Management, a subsidiary of New Huo Group Holdings Limited (01611.HK), made the investment in GaoTeng International Asset Management’s Bitcoin ETF project. The companies will cooperate on digital asset investment products, institutional client services and digital asset wealth management, and may explore tokenized funds and the joint issuance of other digital asset products. GaoTeng International holds Hong Kong Securities and Futures Commission licenses for Type 1, Type 4 and Type 9 regulated activities and is an asset manager backed by investments from Hillhouse Capital Group and Tencent.

data.title: TPG and Corpay to Acquire Bill in Deal Valued at About $6 Billion
data.description:
According to Sina Finance, TPG and Corpay will acquire Bill Holdings in a deal valued at about $6 billion, with TPG taking a majority stake and Corpay a minority stake. Bill's largest shareholder, Starboard Value, has agreed to support the offer of $63.25 per share. The transaction requires regulatory and shareholder approvals and is expected to close in the first half of 2027. Founder René Lacerte will remain CEO after the deal closes.

Bill closed at $57.63 on Monday. Its shares surged after the Financial Times reported that TPG was nearing a deal, then fell 4% in Thursday's after-hours trading to $61.51.

Lacerte said the new partners would provide capital, expertise and strategic support to accelerate product innovation and Bill's AI transformation. On November 5, Bill reported first-quarter revenue rose 13% year over year to $358.3 million. The company went public in 2019 and announced in May that it would cut about 30% of its workforce to improve profitability and focus resources on AI.

Starboard planned to nominate board candidates at Bill's 2025 annual meeting, but the two sides reached a cooperation agreement in October 2025. TPG and Corpay also jointly acquired business payments provider AvidXchange in October 2025.

data.description: According to Bloomberg, stock market winners and losers tied to Jensen Huang’s ouster from Nvidia Corp. are coming into focus after the past week’s turmoil.

data.title: SEC and CFTC Face Potential Turnover as Senate Committees Hear Four Nominees
data.description: Two U.S. Senate committees held hearings on nominees for seats at the SEC and CFTC, with confirmation of the four candidates during the lame-duck session still uncertain. According to PANews, the hearings focused on the SEC's proposed tokenized-stock “innovation exemption” and the CFTC's jurisdiction over prediction markets.

data.title: Anthropic Raises $119.5 Billion in IPO and Private Placement as Underwriters Exercise Overallotment Option
data.description:
Anthropic completed an IPO and concurrent private placement that raised about $119.5 billion, with underwriters fully exercising the overallotment option.

According to Odaily, the IPO issued 1.127 billion Class A ordinary shares at $83 each, including 147 million shares purchased through the overallotment option. The offering raised about $93.5 billion, of which Anthropic received about $91.6 billion, with the remainder going to selling shareholders.

Anthropic also privately issued about 313 million Class N ordinary shares to seven companies, including AMD, Broadcom, Google, Micron, Microsoft, Nvidia and TSMC partner companies, raising about $26 billion. The combined proceeds were about $119.5 billion before underwriting discounts, commissions and other offering expenses. Anthropic shares began trading under the ticker ANT on the Nasdaq Global Select Market on November 19.

data.title: Arthur Hayes Hints at Further Crypto Market Declines, Says Next Stop May Be 'Goblin Town'
data.description: Arthur Hayes wrote, “Next stop … Goblin Town. Buckle up.” According to Odaily, the remark suggested he was bearish on the crypto market’s direction and may expect further declines.

data.title: Polkadot Approves User-Growth Strategy, Plans Polkadot App and DOT-Backed Stablecoin
data.description: Polkadot’s on-chain governance body, DOT DAO, approved a new strategy focused on user growth, including plans for the Polkadot App and a DOT-backed stablecoin. According to PANews, citing GlobeNewswire, referendum No. 1954 passed with 97% approval; the strategy calls for privacy-protecting, login-free products for general users and for value generated by those products to flow back to DOT. The proposal, submitted by the Polkadot Community Foundation (PCF), requires DAO-funded entities to align with the strategy and shifts progress measures from developer numbers to user counts and usage data. The stable-value token series, dotStables, will begin with dotUSD. PCF will launch the Polkadot App, offering private messaging and digital cash features, and oversee global outreach.

data.title: Gold’s Worst Year in More Than a Decade Challenges Safe-Haven Role
data.description: According to Bloomberg, bullion’s worst year in more than a decade has challenged its reputation as a safe haven, showing investors can’t count on it to protect against every kind of market turmoil.

data.title: Bitcoin and Gold Volatility Gauges Rise as U.S. VIX Gains 52% This Month
data.description:
Volatility measures for Bitcoin, gold and U.S. stocks have risen as Bitcoin, equities, gold, copper and currencies linked to commodities have declined, while global demand for safe havens has increased. According to Odaily, the VIX, which tracks 30-day implied volatility for the S&P 500, has gained 52% this month and 81% this quarter to 29.5, its highest level since March; the Volmex Bitcoin Volatility Index is up 23% this month and 40% this quarter at 52.2, while the gold volatility index has risen 10% and 21%, respectively, to 28.7.

These measures reflect options markets’ expectations for future price swings and typically rise when demand for protection increases. In the third quarter, the MOVE U.S. Treasury volatility index climbed 54% from July to September, and the crude oil volatility index rose 21%, amid higher bond yields and turmoil in the Middle East. Greater volatility in U.S. Treasuries, a foundation of the global financial system, can tighten financial conditions and increase demand for safe havens in other markets.

Expectations that funds would flow back into Bitcoin after Anthropic’s listing have not materialized. Spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded net outflows of more than $580 million on Thursday, bringing outflows so far this month to $3.47 billion. With traditional financial markets closed on weekends, continued risk aversion could add selling pressure on Bitcoin and other cryptocurrencies that trade around the clock. Platforms such as Hyperliquid, which offer perpetual contracts tied to traditional assets, may provide an early window into market sentiment. A softer signal from the Federal Reserve that reduces expectations of further rate increases could ease upward pressure on the dollar and support risk assets.

data.title: Polkadot Community Foundation Passes Proposal Supporting New Polkadot App Strategy
data.description:
The Polkadot Community Foundation (PCF) has passed a proposal to support a new community strategy centered on Polkadot App. According to Foresight News, the strategy will focus ecosystem resources on an upcoming Polkadot product platform, with direct user acquisition as a primary goal.

The platform is designed as an application layer that prioritizes user privacy and data rights, allowing users to choose how much data they share. PCF plans to use Polkadot App to provide a mobile-focused solution for private messaging and digital cash payments. The platform will be anchored by the dotStables stablecoin system, beginning with dotUSD, a dollar-tracking asset launched on October 8. It is initially backed by USDT, with plans to later allow token issuance collateralized by DOT.

The proposal calls for shifting funds from general marketing to incentive programs tied to measurable user engagement. The dotStables design is intended to translate user demand into demand for DOT.

data.title: Bitcoin Miner BitFuFu’s Q3 Revenue Falls 79.1% Year Over Year, Net Profit Reaches $24.9 Million
data.description:
Bitcoin miner BitFuFu reported third-quarter revenue of $37.7 million, down 79.1% year over year, while net profit reached $24.9 million. According to Odaily, the revenue decline was driven mainly by weaker cloud-mining demand, lower Bitcoin prices and reduced sales of mining machines; cloud-mining revenue fell 88.8% to $13.8 million. Net profit was supported by $36.5 million in fair-value gains on digital assets and related receivables and payables.

BitFuFu mined 258 BTC through its self-mining operations in the quarter, up 48.3% year over year, and held 1,388 BTC at the end of September.

data.title: OakNorth, Backed by Jared Kushner’s Affinity Partners, Gets Full U.S. Banking Charter
data.description:
According to Sina Finance, British commercial bank OakNorth has obtained a full U.S. banking charter and plans to expand its U.S. lending business. OakNorth said it became the first foreign digital bank to receive a full charter by acquiring Michigan-based Community Unity Bank. Its shareholders include Affinity Partners, the investment firm associated with Jared Kushner, and SoftBank Vision Fund.

OakNorth applied for a U.S. banking license in 2024 and opened a representative office in New York. It agreed to acquire Community Unity Bank in March 2025. About 40% of its new lending last year was in the U.S. market. With the charter, OakNorth can accept deposits and make loans through its U.S. bank, rather than operating through its British entity, and can serve customers in all 50 states.

Chief Executive Rishi Khosla said OakNorth aims to help entrepreneurs by assessing businesses based on their future financial prospects as well as their operating history. Typical customers have annual revenue of $5 million to $100 million. Khosla said the bank serves proven businesses overlooked by traditional lenders in the U.K., and that similar demand exists in the U.S., where such companies mainly rely on community banks. He described U.S. community banks’ processes as slow and their business models as rigid.

Founded in 2015, OakNorth provides credit to businesses in expansion stages. Co-founders Khosla and Joel Perlman met while studying at the London School of Economics and previously founded and sold a financial data analytics company. Their experience with obstacles to business lending led them to identify a gap for companies too large for startup services but not yet eligible for large commercial loans. SoftBank Vision Fund invested in 2019, and Affinity Partners joined in 2024. Khosla said he aspired to be an entrepreneur from around age nine and gained early experience managing investments for the Mittal steel family. Perlman comes from an entrepreneurial family; one of his brothers built Zumba dance classes into a globally known brand.

data.title: Aswath Damodaran Says Nvidia Is 30% Below Fair Value, Would Buy at $140
data.description:
According to Sina Finance, New York University professor and valuation expert Aswath Damodaran said Nvidia’s market capitalization was about 30% below his estimated fair value of $4.8 trillion, implying a break-even value of about $140 per share. He said he had placed a limit buy order at that price and would add Nvidia back to his portfolio if the stock fell to that level.

Damodaran called CEO Jensen Huang an “excellent CEO.” He said that since Huang acknowledged the controversy early last week, Nvidia’s market value had fallen by more than $2 trillion to $3.52 trillion. Nvidia announced last Thursday that Huang had resigned and named CFO Colette Kress interim CEO. The company is still selecting a permanent CEO, and Damodaran said the crisis was not over.

Damodaran said Kress and other internal executives were suitable candidates. He said Apple CEO Tim Cook was not suited to lead Nvidia under current conditions, except perhaps as an interim leader handling the crisis. He also said the management changes and scandal had likely reduced Nvidia’s intrinsic value, cautioning that a falling share price did not necessarily make the stock attractive. He said Huang’s experience showed why even outstanding executives need checks on their authority.

Nvidia shares were down 40% from their early October peak and 21% for the year. Retail investor sentiment on Stocktwits cooled on Friday but remained in the “extremely bullish” range.

data.title: Nvidia Interim CEO Colette Kress Faces ‘Glass Cliff’ as She Addresses Jensen Huang’s Legacy
data.description:
Nvidia interim CEO and CFO Colette Kress has been tasked with addressing problems left by Jensen Huang and faces intense scrutiny, according to Bloomberg. According to Odaily, after Huang’s departure, Kress must handle both CEO and CFO duties, lead an earnings call on short notice, reassure employees, respond to government investigations and balance preserving Huang’s legacy with separating the company from controversies tied to his exit. She also faces management challenges related to Huang family members holding senior positions at the company.

The situation has been described as a “glass cliff,” in which women are more likely to take top roles when companies are in crisis and face greater risks of failure. The technology industry has often portrayed male leaders as charismatic geniuses while casting female executives as “adults in the room” responsible for maintaining order and stability. Some employees and investors have called for Huang to return. Huang has said he would be willing to resume the CEO role if the board asked him to.

data.title: ANTB-Paired Memecoins Eligible for Ecosystem Rewards From Trading Fees

The pool is funded by 10% of eligible internal trading fees, with 40% allocated to qualifying developers and 60% to qualifying holders. The campaign runs Nov 20 to 27.

data.title: Bitcoin News | Bitcoin Falls to $61,300 After Anthropic’s IPO as Nasdaq Futures Slip Below 200-Day Average
data.description: Bitcoin fell to nearly $61,300 late Thursday, near its lowest level since early July, after AI company Anthropic’s shares debuted on Nasdaq and tech stocks weakened. Bitcoin traded around $61,700 on Friday, about 29% below its October high of $87,200. More than $600 million in crypto futures positions were liquidated over 24 hours. Nasdaq futures slipped 0.7% and fell below their 200-day moving average after Thursday’s 2.4% drop in the index.Anthropic Prices Above Range and Closes 17% Higher on DebutAnthropic listed on Nasdaq on November 19 under the ticker ANT. It priced shares at $83, above its $70–$78 range, and raised about $81.3 billion in the offering. Including a $26 billion private placement, the total comes to $107.3 billion. The shares opened at $111.50, 34.3% above the IPO price, and closed their first day at $97.17, up 17.1% (calculated).Crypto Liquidations Top $600 MillionMost major cryptocurrencies fell with bitcoin, including ether, XRP and SOL. Ether traded near $1,748. Nearly half of the $600 million-plus in liquidations came in the last 12 hours, suggesting a rapid unwind of leveraged positions amid the volatility around the IPO.Analysts Split on Whether Capital Will Rotate Back to CryptoSome market participants expect money to flow back into digital assets now that the IPO is done, a view that has persisted through bitcoin’s recent slide.“My sense is that, with the Anthropic IPO now in the rear-view mirror, we could start to see capital rotating back into crypto as Bitcoin tests lower price levels, potentially below $62,000, in the coming weeks,” said Paul Howard, senior director at crypto market maker Wincent. “Rather than expecting a sharp rebound, I would anticipate a more orderly recovery over the winter months, as institutional capital gradually returns and investors look to rebuild exposure at more attractive valuations.”Others warned that continued risk aversion in tech stocks could drag bitcoin lower.“Bitcoin is unlikely to be insulated from a broader reduction in risk appetite,” said Ryan Kirkley, co-founder and CEO of settlement infrastructure firm Global Settlement Network. “When institutions reduce exposure to technology equities, crypto can face similar selling pressure because both remain sensitive to liquidity conditions.”Kirkley added that concerns about AI financing could lead investors to cut leverage and move into more defensive positions, bringing more volatility for digital assets.Long-Term Case Shifts Toward Settlement and TokenizationKirkley said short-term price swings do not weaken the long-term case for blockchain infrastructure. He said the next phase of institutional adoption will depend less on speculative valuations and more on measurable improvements in how capital moves.“Stablecoins, tokenised assets and real-time settlement infrastructure have an opportunity to demonstrate value by reducing friction, improving liquidity management and making financial transactions more efficient,” he said.

data.title: A24’s Box Office Success Could Give HBO Max a Streaming Edge
data.description: According to CNBC, A24 generated more than $526 million at the domestic box office this year as of Nov. 15, roughly $290 million—or more than 50%—above its total for all of 2025. Under a licensing deal renewed in January, HBO Max subscribers in the U.S. can stream new A24 films for a limited period after their theatrical runs. When “Backrooms” began streaming on HBO Max, it was the platform’s most-streamed title for two weeks and drew 226 million minutes of viewing time in its premiere week.
